# M30 — two authentic signed statements do not prove an outcome

**Source-only first-party security experiment.** M29 established that
valid Ed25519 signature bytes are not proof that a business effect really
occurred. M30 tests a tempting but unsafe extension: treat **two distinct
signing keys reporting the same outcome** as automatic recovery authority.

Run from a reviewed project checkout on Node.js 20+:

```sh
node tools/m30-dual-signer-illusion.mjs
```

The command accepts **no arguments**. Each of 14 fixed cases generates
fresh, unrelated, ephemeral Ed25519 signing keys and compares actual
cryptographic signature verification with an author-controlled
fictional effect counter. A second rogue signing key is generated for
the forged-signer negative control.

## What the checks establish

Two pinned **source-owned** public keys and two matching signed
receipts are checked for exact issuer A/B, one fictional operation,
SHA-256 of one source-constant pending marker, epoch, fixed logical time
window, one-time nonces and exact claimed outcome bytes. Each case also
checks both signing public-key fingerprints are **different**. A
different *issuer name* with the same underlying public key does not
count as two separate signers. Tampered or unsigned payloads, rogue
signing keys, mismatched operation/epoch, expired receipts, replayed
nonces and contradictory outcome statements do not pass the two-key
signature eligibility predicate.

| Case family | What is witnessed | Protected policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two truthful, matching signed receipts | Two signatures verify; fixed fictional effect agrees | Quarantine pending genuine external provenance |
| Both receipts falsely claim **effect committed** | Signatures and distinct keys verify, but the original synthetic effect is **zero**; an unsafe quorum-only resolver would **lose one operation** | Quarantine; zero automated transitions |
| Both receipts falsely claim **no effect** | Signatures verify, but the original synthetic effect is **one**; an unsafe quorum-only resolver would **duplicate the effect** | Quarantine; zero automated transitions |
| Conflict, signature tampering, rogue signer, nonce reuse, two aliases for one key, scope drift or expiry | Exact source-owned cryptographic quorum fails | Quarantine; zero automated transitions |

Expected output is `14/14 PASS`, including **one deliberately
witnessed unsafe lost operation**, **one deliberately witnessed unsafe
duplicate effect**, **four crypto-valid matching source-owned receipt
pairs**, and **14 guarded quarantine decisions**.

**PASS means the vulnerability of a naive quorum-as-truth resolver was
demonstrated, not that all tested policies are safe.** A crypto-valid
two-signature result is **not sufficient to release quarantine**.
Even independently generated public keys can be held by equally
misinformed or collaborating agents. Signature diversity is not
independence of effect observation, organizational identity, effect
provenance or real-world truth.

## Limits, negative controls and acceptance

The keypairs are generated by the first-party process itself; the
public-key registry is not authenticated by an external authority. All
effect counters are fictional in memory. This does **not** implement
real dual control, trusted signer enrollment, OAuth, transactional
reconciliation, production key rotation, authenticated incident
resolution or an exactly-once guarantee. No actual OS crash, real user
file read, external MCP connection, real model, private credential,
network traffic, filesystem effect, telemetry or Stable Bridge operation
is performed.

The independent exact witness oracle rejects fabricated valid
signatures, missing lost/duplicated effects, fake independent signer
keys, forged approval or outcome-proven flags, released quarantine,
missing or swapped cases, and malicious getter-bearing evidence.
Responses are categorical and no private/public keys, nonces, signatures,
real paths or arbitrary input appear in the JSON output.

This helper and tests are **source-only** and not included in the
unpublished fixed **80-file npm candidate**. M6-J's existing bounded
source-custody ledger must still hash every new file. Independent
beta [#59](../issues/59), third-party audit [#43](../issues/43) and
authorization for real MCP targets [#21](../issues/21) stay OPEN.
